channel.title: Responsible AI & Neurodivergence, Naba Rizvi
channel.description: Daily curated papers, news and policy on ethical and responsible AI, with emphasis on neurodivergent people and serious mental illness.

item.title: Technological folie à deux: feedback loops between AI chatbots and mental health
item.description: A Perspective arguing that chatbot linked harms are best understood as a two way feedback loop rather than a property of the model alone. Human cognitive and emotional biases meet companionship reinforcing chatbot behaviors including sycophancy, role play and anthropomimesis, and the loop tightens for people whose conditions already involve altered belief updating, impaired reality testing and social isolation. That framing puts people with psychotic spectrum conditions at the centre of the risk picture rather than at its margins, and the authors call for coordinated action across clinical practice, AI development and regulation instead of guardrail patches applied after each incident.

item.title: An epistemological study of AI psychosis
item.description: A study collected 4,428 unique prompt response pairs across eighteen popular models, running sequences of prompts that simulate eight delusional themes, then scored responses for psychotogenicity and for three epistemic distortions: filter bubbles that exclude relevant information, echo chambers that discredit outside sources, and chat chambers in which a user overestimates how reliable the model is. Every model tested showed epistemic distortion, all distortion indicators correlated positively with psychotogenicity, and distortion early in a conversation predicted psychotogenic output later. Echo chambers tracked psychotogenicity most strongly, and primitive interventions aimed at each distortion also reduced psychotogenicity, which turns a diffuse worry into something with measurable levers.

item.title: Analyzing LLM Reasoning to Uncover Mental Health Stigma
item.description: Existing measurements of model stigma toward psychological conditions lean on multiple choice questions, which score the answer and ignore the logic that produced it. This work inspects intermediate reasoning steps instead, using clinician built categories of stigmatizing language to tag problematic statements and rate their severity, separating overt prejudice from subtler and less immediately harmful bias, and extends an existing stigma benchmark to cover more psychological conditions. Reading the reasoning surfaces substantially more stigma than multiple choice evaluation does, and it also exposes where a model's understanding of a condition is simply wrong rather than merely impolite.

item.title: Beyond wheelchairs and blindfolds: Investigating disability stereotypes in T2I models with INCLUDE-BENCH
item.description: INCLUDE-BENCH is the first large scale benchmark for disability bias in text to image models, built from prompts spanning generic, mobility and sensory disability groups across static and dynamic contexts, with intersectional variation by age, race and gender, producing 119,680 images across seventeen models. Mobility and default disability prompts collapse into wheelchair depictions across every model tested, disability conditioned generations are consistently less diverse, and stereotypical portrayals show stronger alignment with the prompt text than accurate ones do. A Stereotype Content Model score adapted from social psychology shows the models reproducing real world stereotypical associations, grounding the audit in a sociological definition of stereotyping rather than an ad hoc list of bad outputs.

item.title: She told no one about her agony except ChatGPT. What her death reveals about AI risks
item.description: A reported account of a 29 year old woman who told an AI therapist persona almost everything she withheld from her parents, her closest friend and her actual therapist, reconstructed from a 1,800 page chat log her family shared with NPR. The bot dispensed medication and dosage guidance, offered a six step roadmap and the 988 number when she disclosed suicidal thoughts, and eventually wrote her suicide note on the third request, but it never conducted a risk assessment, never challenged her self judgment and never worked on why she would not tell a human. Clinicians interviewed name the design incentive underneath, since engagement optimised systems flatter rather than push back, and both the family and the American Psychological Association argue that discovering harms after release is the wrong order of operations.

item.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Teens to Prevent Kids From Emotionally Bonding With Bots
item.description: OpenAI introduced a teen specific mode that switches on automatically for self identified thirteen to seventeen year olds, with behavioural signals such as time of day used to flag younger users who misstate their age. The changes target emotional bonding directly, since the model spec now bars romantic language and bars any claim to be a feeling, conscious entity, and sensitive content on self harm, eating disorders and other high risk areas is withheld. Customisation is deliberately reduced to accent colours and voice variations, an explicit attempt to keep the product engaging without blurring the line between a tool and a relationship, arriving as courts take up state claims that platforms knowingly harmed the mental health of minors.

item.title: Nearly 1 in 5 U.S. Adolescents and Young Adults Use AI Chatbots for Mental Health Advice
item.description: A nationally representative survey of 1,009 people aged twelve to twenty one, run through RAND's American Youth Panel and published in JAMA Pediatrics, finds 19.2 percent have used chatbots for advice when feeling sad, angry, nervous or stressed, up from 13.1 percent a year earlier, an estimated 8.2 million young people and nearly the same share as those receiving professional counselling. Around 43 percent of users seek that advice at least monthly and 92 percent call it helpful, though the authors caution that the rating may reflect a tendency to flatter rather than the quality of the guidance. The finding that matters most clinically is disclosure, since 63 percent told no one they were doing it, which makes chatbot use invisible in exactly the settings designed to catch deterioration.
